reviewer: Claude agent review (Opus), not a human historian
text: 2026-10-23: reviewed the v2 rewrite of story.json to the 2026-10-20 template (twelve scenes, with the new pictures vatapi-rock, the-front and kanchi-gate; scene-08, scene-09 and scene-12 retired) against facts.json, research/badami-chalukya-vikramaditya2-verified.md and badami-chalukya.md, the previous review and bible/style.md; the validator reports only the expected image-set change and the changed illustration disclosure.

One spine, chronological; three named people (ವಿಕ್ರಮಾದಿತ್ಯ, ನಂದಿಪೋತವರ್ಮ, ಲೋಕಮಹಾದೇವಿ) and three years (642, 733/734, 745); the turn (the raised hand at the open gate) is scene 9 and the greatness act (the gold returned and the Kannada pillar) is scene 10; every scene ends on a question the next scene answers; all twelve of the earlier blockers stay fixed.

Fixed on review: a ನಿಮಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತೇ? pointer that no longer resolved; the summary's unsourced 'the spared Pallava rose again'; the content note and illustration disclosure that still spoke of Navsari; the Kuram plates' 'vijaya on Pulikeshi's back' now disclosed as a figure of speech for putting him to flight. Nothing is softened: Nandipotavarman 'fled' as the plate says, and the Rashtrakuta defeat of the son is stated plainly. The introduction gives the vow's cause in the plates' words, and the Kanchi pillar's condition is dated to the 1890s reports.

The three new pictures were checked against the bible and the scene text: the king's face matches the other pictures, and there are no domes, gopurams, firearms or curved swords; boar banners are on the Chalukya side only and bull banners on the Pallava side. The Pallava rock record is shown on a ledge above the lake (it is really behind the Mallikarjuna temple at Badami, much worn), which is disclosed. Nits recorded and not regenerated: the-front and scene-04 have similar compositions and a different jacket colour, and the kanchi-gate gate and the view through it differ from scene-06.

Newcomer test: both answers yes. A reader can say who he was, what he wanted, what happened at Kanchi and why it matters; suspense builds from the camp to the gate, and ಮಥಿಸು, ಘಟಿಗೆ and ನಿವರ್ತನ are glossed. The battle carries no personal danger to the king because no source gives one.

2026-10-15: approved on a third read of story.json (title, teaser, introduction, twelve scenes with paragraphs, alt texts, facts and dramatised lists, summary, ನಿಮಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತೇ?, visitToday, provenance, illustration disclosure, content note), facts.json, outline.md and the collections.json 'badami-chalukya' entry, against research/badami-chalukya-vikramaditya2-verified.md with badami-chalukya-verified.md and badami-chalukya.md where the new file confirms them. The first pass returned twelve text blockers; the second pass found all fixed and two small nits, now also fixed.

First-pass blockers, fixed: (1) Kisuvolal glossed as 'the coronation town' where the family was crowned, contradicting scene-02's anointing at Vatapi; now only 'ಪಟ್ಟದ ಕಿಸುವೊಳಲು' as the old name, Fleet's guessed meaning left to the ನಿಮಗೆ ಗೊತ್ತೇ? box. (2) The Badami Pallava rock record called a different language (it is Sanskrit in Grantha script) and placed behind a Mallikarjuna temple in 733; now 'ಪಲ್ಲವರ ಗ್ರಂಥ ಲಿಪಿ' on 'ವಾತಾಪಿಯ ಗುಡ್ಡದ ಒಂದು ಬಂಡೆ'. (3) An unsourced 'Shiva's dynasty' label; now 'the dynasty that built the Vijayesvara'. (4) 'No house burned' in Kanchi, banned by the outline; cut. (5) 'The king had fled' (asserting Nandipotavarman's flight from his capital, against verified §3f); cut. (6) The temple gold both returned and topped up with the king's own, turning two translations of one word (pratyarpana) into two gifts; now one act, returned, as the Kanchi pillar says. (7) The anivarita thread told as a fact of the scene; now only the plate's 'anivarita pratapa', the thread kept to the hedged box. (8) Both queens' temples said to commemorate the victory and both said to still stand; only the Lokesvara is tied to Kanchi, and Trailokyesvara = Mallikarjuna is disclosed as an identification. (9) 'All the northern kings' broken by the Arab army; now the plate's named kingdoms. (10) Undisclosed Ramayana/Mahabharata reliefs and 'Dravida style'; cut. (11) 'Fifty villages' for the Nareyangal Fifty; now the record's name only. (12) The narrator inviting the reader to weigh Dantidurga's plate; now told as Dantidurga's own act.

Every date, name, number and quotation was compared with the verified file: accession 733 or 734; the vow (anointment, great energy, natural enemy, uprooting root and all, Tundaka-vishaya); Lakshmeshwar Saka 656, January 735, Raktapura, Bahubali, Sankhatirtha basadi, the white Jinalaya, fifty nivartanas, disclosed as a 10th-century Sanskrit copy; Nandipotavarman 'came out to meet him' and was put to flight, not slain; the trophies; Kanchi entered without destroying it and the gifts to the twice-born, the distressed and the helpless; the Kanchi pillar's eleven Kannada lines, curse on the ghatige mahajanas and the scribe Anivaritapunyavallabha, with Hultzsch's 'great probability' disclosed; Pandya, Chola, Kerala, Kalabhra and the unplaced ocean pillar; Navsari 739 or 740, the six kingdoms, the oath, Mirashi's four names, the unnamed overlord, the Banavasi Brahman; Kirtivarman's plea verbatim; Lokamahadevi of the Haihayas, 'mother of mankind', Lokesvara = Virupaksha, Gunda's mume-perjjerepu and Tribhuvanacharya, the Sarvasiddhi titles as Fleet's reading, the singers' covenant and the Nareyangal immunities; Trailokyamahadevi; reign end about 745 with 744/745 against 746/747 disclosed; the 754 eclipse pillar; Samangad via Fleet's summary; the last charter; UNESCO 1987.

The storytelling rule: scene prose is told as events, with no scholar named and no evidence weighed; records appear only as acts in the story (the pillar being cut at Kanchi, the son's charter written later, the Navsari grant, Dantidurga's plate, the 754 pillar). Every silence filled (the battle's day and course, the night of the trophies, the treasury, the southern shore, Navsari's evening, the son's homecoming, Gunda's ceremony, the king reading his title) is disclosed in that scene's dramatised list. The king is never demeaned; the Pallava is credited for meeting him in the field; the Arabs are drawn only from the plate, with no religious framing and no 'first/only/saved India'.

Kannada: adult told-story register; no em dash; NFC; Kannada digits in Kannada text; names consistent (ನಂದಿಪೋತವರ್ಮ, ಅವನಿಜನಾಶ್ರಯ ಪುಲಕೇಶಿ, ಲೋಕಮಹಾದೇವಿ, ತ್ರೈಲೋಕ್ಯಮಹಾದೇವಿ, ಗುಂಡ; ಪುಲಿಕೇಶಿ only for Pulikeshi II). The collections.json entry (Vijayaditya c. 696–733, Vikramaditya II c. 733–745, Kirtivarman II c. 745–757, the refined notes and two added sources) agrees with the verified file.
illustrations: All thirteen WebPs in public/history/badami-chalukya/immadi-vikramaditya/ (cover, scene-01 to scene-12, 1600x900) were opened and compared with scene text, alt and bible/style.md, with enlarged crops of the cover skyline, the scene-02 banners, the scene-03 king, the scene-06 temple tower and the scene-09 commander's sword. The second-pass report that scene-04 to scene-12 were the Kalyani pictures was the reviewer's own error (stale preview files); the published files are this book's renders.

The king is the same man throughout: clean-shaven heart-shaped face, high cheekbones, long straight hair, low fan-fronted ruby crown (a gold fillet as prince in scene-01, a cloth headwrap in camp in scenes 03, 05, 08). He is handsome, strong and upright, and distinct from Pulikeshi, Mayurasharma, Chavundaraya, Amoghavarsha, Vishnuvardhana and Chikkadevaraja. Vijayaditya is grey-bearded; Kirtivarman has a faint moustache.

Bible exclusions hold: boar banners only on the Chalukya side (the Pallava line carries bull banners in scene-04); the cover was re-rendered so that the Kanchi skyline shows tiled roofs and one pyramidal temple tower, with no domes; no towering gopuram at Kanchi (scene-06's distant tower is a single-finial vimana); no later mandapa in the Kailasanatha (scene-07); no crescent, modern Arab dress or sinister faces at Navsari, and straight swords on the Indian side (scene-09); no gore, no captives, the Pallava withdrawal orderly. Scene-05 shows the khatvanga skull-club standard among the captured Pallava insignia, as the verified file's khatvanga-dhvaja allows and as scene-05's dramatised list discloses.

Nits recorded and not regenerated: scene-03's flat jewelled headwrap and quilted jacket (as prompted) sit close to the 'no turbans on royalty' exclusion; scene-06's banners are carried upright though the prose has them lowered, and its temple tower is taller than the alt's 'low frontage'; on the cover the banners are raised; scene-11's queen wears a stitched blouse; scene-12 shows the 754 pillar beside the two queens (the pillar itself is of Kirtivarman's reign).
limitations: This is an AI review by a Claude agent; no human historian or epigraphist has read the text or checked the images.

Fact checking was limited to research/badami-chalukya-vikramaditya2-verified.md and its companion files (Fleet 1896 and IA VII and X, Kielhorn EI V, Hultzsch SII I and EI III, Pathak EI IX, Bhagwanlal 1888, Mirashi CII IV in short quotations, Elliot and Dowson I); the Samangad grant was read only through Fleet's summary; Pallava records of Nandivarman's side were not opened.
No portrait of Vikramaditya II, his queens or Gunda survives; the faces are AI reconstructions, dressed after the Pattadakal reliefs of his reign.
The Mallikarjuna identification of Trailokyesvara rests on the UNESCO nomination and was not re-checked; the present state of the Kanchi pillar rests on Hultzsch's reports of 1890 and 1895.
Images were judged at 1600x900 WebP with enlarged crops; small distant details could not all be verified individually, and the nits above remain.
